Question:
Given points \(P_1,\) \(P_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(P_7\) on a straight line, in the order stated (not necessarily evenly spaced). Let \(P\) be an arbitrarily selected point on the line and let \(s\) be the sum of the undirected lengths

\[ PP_1,\ PP_2,\ \ldots,\ PP_7. \]

Then \(s\) is smallest if and only if the point \(P\) is:
Solution:
Pair the first point with the last, the second with the sixth, and the third with the fifth. For any two points \(A,B\) on the line,
\[
PA+PB\ge AB.
\]
If \(P\) lies between \(A\) and \(B\), segment addition gives equality; outside that segment, the trip through \(P\) is longer.

Applying this observation to the three pairs gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
PP_1+PP_7&\ge P_1P_7,\\
PP_2+PP_6&\ge P_2P_6,\\
PP_3+PP_5&\ge P_3P_5.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(S_0=P_1P_7+P_2P_6+P_3P_5\). Adding the three bounds and the remaining distance yields
\[
s\ge S_0+PP_4.
\]
At \(P=P_4\), the point lies between the endpoints of every pair, so all three bounds are equalities and \(PP_4=0\). Hence \(s=S_0\).

If \(P\ne P_4\), then \(PP_4>0\), and the displayed bound gives \(s>S_0\). Therefore the minimum occurs if and only if \(P=P_4\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
